[USER] User inquired about the possibility of a piece of music having a melody without harmony or vice versa.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Yes, it’s possible for a piece of music to have a melody without harmony or vice versa.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Melody without harmony: Music has a single line of notes played or sung one after the other, with no accompaniment. Examples include traditional folk songs or a cappella singing.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Harmony without melody: Found in instrumental music where multiple notes are played simultaneously without a clear melody. An example is a drone, a continuous note or chord played on a bagpipe or a tanpura.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Most commonly, music has both melody and harmony, which complement each other to create a more immersive musical experience.  
[USER] User expressed interest in examples of popular songs with a strong melody but minimal harmony.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] An example of a song with a strong melody but minimal harmony is "My Heart Will Go On" by Celine Dion from the movie Titanic.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The melody of "My Heart Will Go On" is simple but powerful, with the accompaniment consisting mainly of sustained chords played on a keyboard, providing minimal harmony.  
[USER] User requested another example of a song with no harmony to explore the idea further.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] An example of a song without any harmony is “Amazing Grace,” typically performed a cappella with only one voice singing the melody.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] While different harmonies have been added to “Amazing Grace” over the years, the original melody is strong enough to stand on its own without any accompaniment or harmony.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Another example of a song with minimal harmony is "The Sound of Silence" by Simon & Garfunkel.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The melody of "The Sound of Silence" stands out on its own, with the harmony consisting mainly of sustained chords played on a guitar, emphasizing the emotional power of the lyrics and melody.
